newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-ITALIAN SCHEDULED MATCHES FOR THURSDAY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ITALIAN SCHEDULED MATCHES FOR THURSDAY.

text.p: Serie A matches due to be played on Thursday, all games kick-off 18.30 GMT:

Swede Nils Liedholm, 74, is still looking for his first win since taking over Roma last month. He may have to wait a bit longer against an Atalanta side handicapped by the absence of three suspended players, defender Walter Bonacina, midfielder Paolo Foglio and schemer Domenico Morfeo. Roma may drop Argentine striker Abel Balbo, replacing him with Marco Delvecchio or Francesco Totti in attack.

Although in the relegation zone, Cagliari can take a major step towards ensuring Serie A survival if they beat Fiorentina. Roberto Muzzi returns for Cagliari to partner Sandro Tovalieri in attack while disheartened Fiorentina, beaten Cup Winners' Cup semi-finalists, look to their unsettled Argentine super star, Gabriel Batistuta in attack.

Inter should pick up three easy home points against a side already relegated. They have their first choice strike force of Frenchman Youri Djorkaeff, Chilean Ivan Zamorano and Maurizio Ganz available. Reggiana look to Massimo Minetti and Russian Igor Simutenkov to salvage pride.

Leaders Juventus will give nothing away to relegation battlers Piacenza, just three days before they meet second placed Parma in a game which could decide the league title contest. Defender Ciro Ferrara is suspended and will be replaced by Sergio Porrini alongside Mark Juliano, Alessio Tacchinardi and Portugal's Manuel Dimas in defence, while Christian Vieri and Croat Alen Boksic lead the attack. Piacenza will be without suspended defender Fausto Pari but welcome back midfielder Giuseppe Scienza behind Gian Pietro Piovani and Pasquale Luiso in attack.

Since taking over at Lazio at the beginning of February, coach Dino Zoff has picked up 24 of a possible 36 points and that positive run may continue against a Napoli side missing its Brazilian midfielders, Beto and Andre Cruz. Italian internationals Pierluigi Casiraghi and Giuseppe Signori lead the Lazio attack, while ex-Lazio player Massimiliano Esposito partners Nicola Caccia up front for Napoli.

Parma have to win to keep up the pressure on leaders Juventus, against whom they play a potentially all-decisive game in Turin on Sunday. Parma are without Croat midfielder Mario Stanic but field Argentine Hernan Crespo and Enrico Chiesa in attack while Milan field the awesome duet of Liberian George Weah and Roberto Baggio in attack.

All is not yet lost for relegation battlers Perugia, so this promises to be a bitter dogfight against a Bologna side looking for UEFA points. Croat Milan Rapajic and Marco Negri again lead the Perugia attack while Bologna, as ever, look to Swede Kennet Andersson, this time partnered by Davide Fontolan.

Giant killers Udinese were told this week by coach Alberto Zaccheroni to "close their eyes and put the foot down on the accelerator". Verona, a side relegated in all but mathematical certainty, are unlikely to provide any red lights along the road to a UEFA Cup spot. Paolo Poggi, Brazilian Amoroso and German Oliver Bierhoff lead the impressive Udinese attack while Verona look to Filippo Maniero and Nicola Zanini.

These are just two of eight sides still in the fight for UEFA places, excluding Juventus and Parma, the first and second. Roberto Murgita leads the Vicenza attack while Sampdoria must do without defenders David Balleri and Marco Franceschetti as well as Argentine midfielder Juan Veron, all suspended. Roberto Mancini and Vincenzo Montella lead the Sampdoria attack.
